newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside sees gradual Cossack restart.
newsitem.headline: Woodside sees gradual Cossack restart.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd on Wednesday said it expected to restart the gas export system of its Cossack Pioneer offshore crude oil facility on Friday, enabling it to gradually restore crude oil production.
Output from Cossack Pioneer was reduced to about 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) from its designed 115,000 barrels capacity in early October in order to perform repair work on the export system.
"We are confident that we will be able to meet all our shipping orders," a Woodside spokesman said.
He could not give a specific date when the platform would reach its full producing capacity.

Cossack Pioneer, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields in the North West Shelf, has been plagued by weather-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year.
Normal production is reported to be around 90,000 bpd.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are Woodside, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd and units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
